newsitem.title: FRANCE: France lends support to Bosnia's Plavsic.
newsitem.headline: France lends support to Bosnia's Plavsic.

text.p: France on Wednesday voiced support for Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic in her power struggle with hardliners of the ruling Serb Democratic Party (SDS) party obstructing the peace process.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said France "cannot tolerate persons indicted by the international criminal tribunal having a role in political life" -- a clear reference to former president Radovan Karadzic, an indicted war criminal.
Plavsic has accused the SDS, which is covertly led by Karadzic, of trying to oust her.

Relations between Plavsic and the SDS leadership reached a crisis at the weekend when she tried to dismiss the interior minister for refusing to investigate alleged corruption linked to companies run by Karadzic.
The SDS said Plavsic acted unconstitutionally and ordered her to comply or hand over power.

"Mrs Plavsic has showed her desire to participate in peace efforts in Bosnia-Herzegovina...We ask the (Bosnian Serb) Republic to conform to the Dayton peace accords," Rummelhardt told a daily news briefing.
"Trying war criminals before the war crimes tribunal is one of our main preoccupations," he said.
Plavsic was elected president last year when the international community forced Karadzic to renounce public office. It has not been able to prevent him wielding power behind the scenes.
Diplomats have said it would be a setback for the fragile peace process if Karadzic succeeded in toppling Plavsic, a wartime hardliner who has since become more pragmatic.
